title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol: God knows Gospel benefits will harm reprobates and decreed not to add softening grace — yet preaching is not from primary intention a medium of damnation
pass_a_gloss: We grant indeed that God knows that the preaching of the Gospel, and all his other benefits, will be noxious unto these reprobate; we grant further that the will of no reprobate is so wild and so intractable that God cannot soften it unto faith and penitence (that is, unto the effect of obeying); we grant finally that God has decreed with himself not to apply unto these reprobate that special and efficacious grace by which they would be softened: But all these things being posited we deny that either the preaching of the Gospel, or that gift of a scantier and more common grace, is proposed from a primary and nearest intention of damning, or ought to be judged as media subordinated unto damnation. For we ought not from foresight, or permission of God, or from a following event to infer that the primary intention of God, and the subordination of media, looked unto producing such an event.
pass_b_english: We grant God knows Gospel preaching and his other benefits will be harmful to these reprobates. We grant further that no reprobate's will is so wild and intractable that God cannot soften it to faith and penitence — that is, to the effect of obeying. We grant finally that God has decreed with himself not to apply to these reprobates that special efficacious grace by which they would be softened. All that granted, we still deny that Gospel preaching, or that gift of scantier commoner grace, is proposed from a primary nearest intention of damning, or ought to be judged media subordinated to damnation. From foresight, or God's permission, or a following event, we may not infer that God's primary intention, and the subordination of media, aimed at producing that event.
source_text: Concedimus quidem, Deum scire Evangelii praedicationem, aliaque omnia sua beneficia hisce reprobatis fore noxia; concedimus insuper, nullius reprobati voluntatem tam feram tamque intratabilem esse, quin possit Deus illam ad fidem et poenitentiam (hoc est, ad obediendi effectum) emollire; concedimus denique, Deum decrevisse apud se hisce reprobatis non apponere illam gratiam specialem et efficacem, qua emollirentur: Sed hisce omnibus positis negamus, aut Evangelii praedicationem, aut illam parcitoris et communioris gratiae donationem ex primaria et proxima intentione damnandi proponi, aut tanquam media damnationi subordinata judicari oportere. Non enim debemus ex praevisione, aut permissione Dei, aut ex eventu subsequente inferre primariam Dei intentionem, et mediorum subordinationem ad talem eventum producendum spectasse.
